$description: The layer application code should use. Every token names a JOB, not a colour — so the same markup works in both themes and a future rebrand touches only this file. Dark values live alongside light ones under $extensions so the two can never drift apart.

surface.$description: The page card — what content sits on.

surface-sunken.$description: The ground behind the card and sidebar.

surface-subtle.$description: Table heads and row hover. 259 uses.

surface-inverse.$description: Primary buttons and the mobile FAB. Flips in dark — light-on-dark becomes dark-on-light.

surface-inverse-hover.$description: Primary button hover. Light lifts zinc-950 to zinc-800; dark drops zinc-50 to zinc-200 — both move AWAY from the page, which is what reads as a press-ready state.

scrim.$description: The dimmed layer behind a modal, drawer or sheet. Stays dark in BOTH themes — deriving it from `fg` would make it white in dark, which lights the page up instead of pushing it back.

border.$description: The default hairline. zinc-950 at 10% (white at 10% in dark) rather than a solid step, so it reads correctly over any surface. 212 uses.

divider.$description: A rule BETWEEN items inside a container, as opposed to the container's own edge. Deliberately lighter than `border` (zinc-950 at 5% vs 10%) — a divider that matches the outer border makes a panel read as a table.

border-strong.$description: Cards that must read as raised — stat tiles, the active nav item.

fg-body.$description: Running copy in rows and cells. 309 uses.

fg-muted.$description: Labels, meta, subtitles. 850 uses — the single most-used class in the app.

fg-subtle.$description: Resting icon colour and timestamps. 438 uses.

accent.$description: Links and informational emphasis. Settles the blue-409 vs indigo-438 split.

focus-ring.$description: Kept identical in both themes — it must read against every surface, and blue-500 already was the Catalyst focus colour.

success-tint.$description: Badge and alert background. Light uses the fixed 100 step; dark uses 15% of the base over the surface, so one rule covers both themes without a second hand-tuned ramp.

success-wash.$description: Large-surface fill for the success tone — alert strips, banners. Deliberately lighter than `success-tint`: the same hue needs more saturation to register in a badge than it does across a whole alert, so a tint used at panel size reads as shouting.

warning-wash.$description: Large-surface fill for the warning tone — alert strips, banners. Deliberately lighter than `warning-tint`: the same hue needs more saturation to register in a badge than it does across a whole alert, so a tint used at panel size reads as shouting.

danger-wash.$description: Large-surface fill for the danger tone — alert strips, banners. Deliberately lighter than `danger-tint`: the same hue needs more saturation to register in a badge than it does across a whole alert, so a tint used at panel size reads as shouting.

on-danger.$description: Text on a filled danger surface. Dark flips to a near-black because `danger` lightens to red-400 there — white on red-400 is 2.87:1 and fails AA. Mirrors how on-accent is handled.

accent-wash.$description: Large-surface fill for the accent tone — alert strips, banners. Deliberately lighter than `accent-tint`: the same hue needs more saturation to register in a badge than it does across a whole alert, so a tint used at panel size reads as shouting.

neutral-tint.$description: The default badge, for states with no semantic charge.
